glosses: to show up, to turn up

stawiać się gdzieś; przychodzić gdzieś

To appear, arrive, or attend, especially suddenly or erratically.

examples.text: Please come on time; don't just show up whenever you feel like it.
No matter how many I throw away, more copies always show up.

“We showed up. We showed up,” Mr. Biden said at a news conference at the United Nations summit on climate change, known as COP26, in Glasgow, Scotland. “The fact that China is trying to assert, understandably, a new role in the world as a world leader, not showing up? Huh. The single most important thing that’s gotten the attention of the world is climate.”

glosses: To be easily visible; to be conspicuous.

examples.text: Stains really show up on this white tablecloth.

glosses: To make visible; to expose.

examples.text: This bright light shows up the dust in the corners of the room.
I bet the Jayhawk fast break could show up the Nimrod's lack of speed.

glosses: To make visible or expose faults and deficiencies in, usually by outdoing, outperforming, or outcompeting another.

examples.text: I finished in five minutes and she showed me up by finishing in three.
His team were not outclassed but, once again, England have reminded us of their habit of being shown up as soon as they face half-decent opposition and one or two authentic category-A footballers.

glosses: To produce an impression on observers; to come off.

examples.text: A pleasing countenance showing above a suit of clothes is attractive and makes the suit show up well, while a face with a blank expression is likely to make a man say to himself, "Well if that man's clothes is going to make me look like that I don't want any of them."

glosses: To show up; to appear suddenly or unexpectedly.

examples.text: Is this your t-shirt that turned up in my drawer?
I don't like people turning up without an appointment.

Highly providential was the appearance on the scene of Corny Kelleher when Stephen was blissfully unconscious but for that man in the gap turning up at the eleventh hour the finis might have been that he might have been a candidate for the accident ward […]
I haven't booked, so I don't have a clue as to whether the service will be busy or not. Supposedly, reservations are compulsory, but I want to find out what would happen if you just turn up.

glosses: To cause to appear; to find by searching, etc.

examples.text: I spent hours in the archives, but couldn't turn up anything on the alleged criminal.

glosses: To increase the amount of something by means of a control, such as the volume, heat, or light.

examples.text: Turn up the radio and sing along.

Turn the rhythm up, don't you wanna just
Come along for the ride?

glosses: To reposition by rotating, flipping, etc., upwards.

examples.text: He turned up his collar against the cold.

glosses: To belay or make fast (a line on a cleat or pin).

examples.text: Turn up the main halyard.

glosses: To party hard, especially when involving alcohol or drugs.

examples.text: We're going to turn up at the concert tonight.

glosses: To acquit.

examples.text: Thirty-six were cast for death, and only one was ‘topped’ (hanged), the very one that expected to be ‘turned up’ (acquitted) for highway robbery.

glosses: Alternative spelling of turn-up.

glosses: To come or be in sight; to be in view; to become visible.

examples.text: And God[…]said, Let[…]the dry land appear.

examples.text: A great writer appeared at that time.

glosses: To stand in presence of some authority, tribunal, or superior person, to answer a charge, plead a cause, etc.; to present oneself as a party or advocate before a court, or as a person to be tried.

examples.text: We must all appear before the judgment seat.
